name: A large or growing journal cannot exhaust a MetroPlat work peer's heap
asks: We have real production systems that are currently dead or half dead.

x-provenance.recorded-by: production-health session (session_013hpeWbbDDrzGAgw8JJGDQG), dispatched by the orchestrator
x-provenance.basis: The Bare Cedar Fog MetroPlat ran out of its 512 MB heap about 20 minutes after start (journal: readEavtEntriesSince/structuredClone/projectValue under query-semantic-records). This is the engineering requirement the Leader's 'dead or half dead' production systems ask of the journal read path.
x-provenance.conversion: pending: to be re-recorded as signed predication cells (@red-cup-engineering/signcell) through record-semantic-record once the orchestrator issues the canonical call; this JSON is the requirement.schema.json carrier until then.
x-provenance.relayed-not-quoted: The Leader's words reach this record through the orchestrator's dispatch, which quotes them; the originating Leader session was not located.

board-opening.need: A work peer's semantic-record queries hold a bounded heap however large its journals grow.

requirements.says: The semantic-record query, and the journal reads beneath it, shall hold the work peer within the FeltOS node's memory budget whatever the size of the journals it reads: at most 32 MB of JavaScript memory (heapUsed + external + arrayBuffers) once started and 64 MB while starting.
requirements.rationale: The work peer died of heap exhaustion: 'production systems that are currently dead or half dead'. The budget is the Leader's (requirement feltos-runs-in-32-mb-with-a-64-mb-startup-peak, 2026-10-10), not a heap cap an agent chose.

requirements.says: The semantic-record query shall not keep a separate copy of a record for each category set it is asked about.
requirements.rationale: The unbounded cache multiplied records per category combination.

requirements.says: A synthetic journal larger than the budget shall prove R1 in the package's tests.
requirements.rationale: Proof against a large journal, not only the committed records.

sources.session: orchestrator session session_01NK9NsqzGweReSgA8X8VBif, production-health dispatch to session_013hpeWbbDDrzGAgw8JJGDQG
sources.words: We have real production systems that are currently dead or half dead. We have lots of sites that are not working properly. We don't have continuous improvement, deployment ... No one is communicating through message channels or even using fallback systems. Fallback systems aren't being updated to reflect what's going on in the primary systems.

corrected.by: Red Cup Engineer Senior office (scheduled session, Claude)
corrected.what: R1's 'configured heap budget' was being read as the node's 512 MB --max-old-space-size, an agent-derived figure. R1 now states the Leader's budget: 32 MB of JavaScript memory once started, 64 MB while starting. The 512 MB in the basis is the cap the node died at, kept as history, not a target.
corrected.signed-cell: The sign-cell below records the text before this correction; the requirement must be re-recorded on the machine (group-requirements) so its signed cell carries R1 as corrected.

budget.measure: heapUsed + external + arrayBuffers, RSS reported beside it
